transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Olivia Park (AtlasHealth Eng Manager), Rohit Sharma (AtlasHealth Backend), Lea Kim (AtlasHealth SRE)

Summary:
Weekly POC sync focused on reliability incident follow-up: a 5xx spike and higher-than-expected timeouts during last week's ramping tests. Reviewed telemetry, hypothesized root causes (client retry storm + transient kernel OOMs + rate-limiter tuning), agreed on immediate mitigations and next steps: log captures, traffic profile sharing, schedule a dedicated throughput test, and finalize retry/backoff policy.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and concrete examples of timeouts/5xxs
- Rate limiting and client-side retries (exponential backoff vs fixed)
- Redwood runtime behavior under prefix cache churn and KV cache misses
- Autoscaling and dedicated capacity options vs host fallback
- Monitoring and alert tuning

----- Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) -----
00:00 Maya Chen: okay hello everyone, thanks for joining the POC weekly. we're gonna focus mostly on the reliability incident from last week. diego and i will run through what we saw, then olivia and team can add what they saw on their side.
00:12 Olivia Park: hi all, thanks. we had a number of 5xx responses in the morning ramp test, and then a lot of client timeouts. it looked like things recovered after about 10 minutes but it did impact the pilot metrics.
00:24 Diego Alvarez: yeah i pulled the initial dashboard. there's a clear spike in 5xx starting around 03:10 UTC on 2025-05-18 and it lasted ~12 minutes. latency p95 jumped as well; we saw retries from your side that correlated with a burst in qps.
00:37 Rohit Sharma: to confirm, our client retried with a naive fixed-interval retry at the moment. we were trying to be aggressive to hit the SLA. looks like that may have made things worse.
00:48 Lea Kim: our alerts fired for error rate; we saw kernel OOM logs on the GPU host around the same window. the error messages are a little noisy so not 100% sure if it's runtime or model memory.
01:02 Diego Alvarez: interesting, we saw OOM-ish traces in the inference runtime too. there are two possibilities: Q1, a memory spike from the model due to longer inputs in that window; Q2, a buildup in KV cache churn causing memory pressure.
01:18 Maya Chen: quick note — sometimes Fireflies messes with names but when we say 'Redwood Dedicate' we mean Redwood Dedicated runtime pool.
01:23 Olivia Park: ha, yeah.
01:24 Diego Alvarez: also worth noting: your traffic profile showed several large batch requests around 03:11 that were longer sequences; those can expand working set and push the host.
01:37 Rohit Sharma: i can share the exact payloads. there was a manual test from our analytics team that included long history context, probably the culprit.
01:45 Maya Chen: good. so we're triangulating client retries + large payload + memory pressure. there's also the rate-limiter: during the spike we saw token-based rate limiting kicking in, which returned 429s for a few clients and then forced retries. if many clients retry quickly, that amplifies load.
02:02 Lea Kim: our retry implementation didn't use jitter; it retried every 500ms up to 6 times.
02:07 Diego Alvarez: yep that's classic retry storm. recommended pattern is exponential backoff with jitter; Redwood defaults we typically suggest start at 200-500ms with full jitter and cap. we'll share the snippet.
02:20 Olivia Park: can you share the specific rate-limit settings you observed on your side?
02:25 Diego Alvarez: sure, during the incident the host returned 429s with header X-RateLimit-Limit: 2000 and X-RateLimit-Remaining around 0 for a short period. The per-tenant token bucket was draining because of concurrent large requests.
02:42 Rohit Sharma: is there an internal queue? our engineers saw some requests fall into a queue and then hit a timeout.
02:49 Diego Alvarez: the Redwood runtime uses a combination of prefix caching and a scheduler that batches by sequence length. When mem pressure rises the scheduler tightens batch size which can increase per-request latency and cause client timeouts. There's also a request queue; if the queue grows past configured SLO we trigger early 5xx to protect the runtime.
03:11 Maya Chen: so immediate mitigations we can do: one, patch client retries to exponential backoff with jitter; two, add a temporary cap on max input tokens for the pilot; three, adjust token rate-limiter thresholds or increase dedicated capacity for the peak window.
03:28 Olivia Park: on our side we'll update retries and push a hotfix to client lib. timeline for that?
03:33 Rohit Sharma: i can make the change today and roll to staging, then to pilot by tomorrow morning.
03:38 Lea Kim: we'll also add alerting for GPU mem pressure with clearer thresholds so we can act faster.
03:45 Diego Alvarez: i'll grab the runtime logs: kernel stack, memory arena, and the scheduler traces. i'll put them in the shared drive. look for a folder named "5xx-20250518-spike".
03:58 Maya Chen: excellent. question from the AtlassHealth product side — sorry AtlasHealth, drop — regarding retries: is it safer to default to fewer retries or to tune server-side queueing?
04:12 Diego Alvarez: both. fewer retries reduce amplified load; server-side queueing and circuit-breakers prevent overload but require capacity headroom. For pilot we often do client-side first because it's quick.
04:25 Priya Nair: Priya here — from a customer success angle, we also recommend a canary gradual roll when changing retry behavior so you don't mask an underlying issue.
04:36 Olivia Park: that makes sense.
04:38 Rohit Sharma: on the point about dedicated capacity, what are the quick numbers? if we move to a 2-GPU Dedicated pool for peak, can we avoid this?
04:49 Maya Chen: Diego, do you want to take that?
04:52 Diego Alvarez: quick calc: on the model config you've been using (a 30B-ish open model), with our quantization and concurrent request patterns, a single A100-class GPU handled ~400 steady qps with typical short sequences. But once sequence lengths increase it's closer to 150-200 qps. A 2-GPU Dedicated pool with burst capacity will give you headroom and reduce queueing — but it's not a silver bullet if client retry storms persist.
05:18 Olivia Park: understood. we'll run the retry change first and then plan the Dedicated test.
05:24 Maya Chen: perfect. another note — we found a few malformed requests that bypassed some validation and forced longer tokenization time; we'll add a validation rule to the SDK.
05:35 Rohit Sharma: thanks. about monitoring — can you export the exact grafana dashboard and the query for the 5xx spike?
05:41 Diego Alvarez: yes, i'll share the dashboard link and the raw prometheus queries.
05:46 Lea Kim: can we also get access to span traces? our tracing system will correlate better with our side logs.
05:52 Diego Alvarez: we'll produce a zip of traces for the window; note that some trace IDs were sampled — we'll include what we have.
06:01 Olivia Park: ok, let's be explicit on ownership. who does what and by when?
06:05 Maya Chen: action items we listed in the doc, but i'll read them: diego will upload runtime logs by friday 5/22; rohit will send payload examples by 5/21; lea will prepare alert thresholds and postmortem template by 5/23; maya will send pricing and dedicated test proposal by 5/22.
06:22 Rohit Sharma: ok noted. one more technical question — during the 5xx we saw "NVidia kernel preemption" in the logs, is that a driver-level issue?
06:33 Diego Alvarez: the log string looked like kernel scheduler preemption events. Could be driver-level or GPU memory contention. we're going to correlate with GPU metrics (fb_memory_usage and compute utilization) during the spike.
06:44 Lea Kim: i'll forward the SRE screenshot where we saw GPU memory climb to 98% for a host.
06:50 Maya Chen: that's consistent. final item — rate limiter behavior: we can temporarily increase per-tenant token bucket for your pilot so it doesn't trip during scheduled testing. Maya to send the proposal.
07:02 Olivia Park: that would help for the scheduled throughput test.
07:05 Priya Nair: scheduling note — we propose the dedicated throughput test mid next week to allow time to implement client retry changes.
07:12 Maya Chen: yes, propose Wed 05/28 14:00 UTC. diego can run the test with you and we can instrument extra telemetry.
07:21 Rohit Sharma: works for us.
07:23 Olivia Park: works.
07:25 Maya Chen: great. any open concerns?
07:28 Lea Kim: just one — can you doc recommended backoff params? our default life cycle is to keep retries limited to 3 and jitter. is there a Redwood recommended snippet?
07:37 Diego Alvarez: yes, we'll share a snippet. Rough recommendation: retry up to 4 times, base delay 200ms, exponential factor 2, full jitter, max delay 5s. For 429 specifically, consider longer cap and token bucket-aware backoff.
07:55 Rohit Sharma: do you have recommendations for alert thresholds for queue length?
07:58 Diego Alvarez: recommended early warning at queue > 50ms average wait or queue length > 100 requests for > 1 minute. exact numbers depend on model and capacity; we'll give tuned defaults in the doc.
08:16 Maya Chen: ok we're at wrap. i'll send the notes, the pricing for Dedicated burst, and the meeting minutes. diego will upload logs/traces. rohit will send payloads. lea will prepare postmortem template. priya will coordinate the throughput test scheduling.
08:31 Olivia Park: thanks everybody. helpful — we'll talk after rohit uploads traces.
08:36 Maya Chen: thanks all, bye.
